transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-08-19
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jamie (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Ari (Aurora PM), Leah (Cloud Integrations), Tom (Marketplace PM), Priya (Security)

Summary:
Quick technical sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for AuroraCloud managed offering with Redwood inference, and next steps for sandbox validation. Focus on VPC connectivity, KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML, billing integration and co-marketing assets.

Topics:
- Marketplace listing metadata & timeline
- Reference architecture (VPC, routing, private deployments)
- Security artifacts (SOC2, KMS, audit logs)
- Validation plan & sandbox testing
- Co-marketing and joint PR timeline

Action items (recorded above)

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Liu: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll kick off, i'm jamie from redwood, carlos is our se — go ahead carlos quick intro?
[00:08] Carlos Mendes: yeah hey all carlos here, i'll be owning the reference arch and the infra runbook, happy to walk through the technical reqs.
[00:14] Ari Patel: thanks jamie, appreciate it. tom and leah and priya are on from aurora, we'll do brief intros — tom runs their marketplace ux, leah handles integrations and priya is our security lead.
[00:24] Tom O'Neill: hi folks, quick note — timeline is pretty tight, aurora wants a sandbox listing by end of month for their marketplace sprint.
[00:31] Leah Kim: yes we have an internal milestone 2026-09-07 for validation, so earlier the better.
[00:37] Jamie Liu: totally — goal today is to align on what we need to hand off so you can submit the listing: metadata, diagrams, security docs, and an integration test plan.

[00:54] Carlos Mendes: first technical note: there are two reference-arch options we typically present — a hosted integration (Redwood hosted API with marketplace billing + connector for private networking) and a private deployment option (Aurora-managed VPC + customer-owned keys). the marketplace tends to prefer the hosted listing for quick time-to-market but some customers will need the private variant.
[01:15] Ari Patel: that matches what we heard, marketplace prefers a single listing with 2 options, is that feasible?
[01:22] Carlos Mendes: yes, we can produce a single listing that documents both "Hosted - Redwood" and "Private - Aurora-managed" flavors. the reference arch will show both flows.

[01:35] Priya Rao: on security — our compliance team will want SOC2 artifacts, KMS integration details, what logs you surface, retention periods, and SAML metadata for SSO into aurora console. can you summarize what redwood exposes?
[01:48] Jamie Liu: yep; we have SOC2 report and ISO summary, i'll share slides. we expose request-level audit logs, per-token cost telemetry, model/route audit trails and optional request/response logging with redaction. defaults are 30 day retention but enterprise can extend.
[02:05] Priya Rao: ok can you provide a matrix of logs vs retention vs PII handling?
[02:10] Jamie Liu: yes that's action item — i'll send the security checklist and matrix.

[02:20] Carlos Mendes: technical detail re: private deployment — our private deployment supports VPC peering and private endpoints. typical pattern: aurora provisioning creates a peered VPC, we provide an endpoint/service in customer VPC; KMS can be customer-managed via an HSM-backed KMS; we also support bringing-your-own-key for model encryption at rest.
[02:42] Leah Kim: when you say endpoint, do you mean a private IP in our VPC or an internal load balancer? we need specifics for our network team.
[02:50] Carlos Mendes: great question — for the private flavor we use an internal NLB with a private IP range, we document ports and health-checks in the runbook. i'll include the terraform snippet in the reference arch repo.

[03:06] Tom O'Neill: marketplace listing requires a short product description, logo, screenshots and an integration quickstart. can redwood provide a quickstart that matches aurora's one-click deploy?
[03:16] Jamie Liu: yes we can produce a quickstart template and a one-click terraform module that aurora can reference. it will be in the repo link we share (link: https://redwood.example.com/marketplace/aurora/ref-arch).

[03:30] Ari Patel: what about billing integration — we need metrics to attribute usage back to aurora for marketplace revenue split.
[03:38] Jamie Liu: marketplace billing options: 1) aurora takes marketplace revenue and invoices customers; 2) we bill directly and share usage metering for revenue share. we can emit per-listing usage files via s3 or push to aurora's billing API.
[03:53] Priya Rao: from security perspective we prefer minimal shared PII in billing exports.
[03:58] Jamie Liu: we'll share a minimal usage schema (tenant id, tokens consumed, cost, timestamp) — no PII by default.

[04:10] Carlos Mendes: another note on latency expectations — hosted option average p95 is 120-220ms for small prompt workloads on our curated models; private dedicated GPU setups obviously vary by infra. for marketplace customers we should set expectations in the listing.
[04:29] Leah Kim: that p95 range is fine as long as it's documented and we can point to a benchmark. can we get a benchmark sheet?
[04:34] Jamie Liu: yes, carlos will share the benchmark spreadsheet (demo synthetic loads across sequence lengths).

[04:44] Tom O'Neill: for the listing UI we also need a short table of SLAs, e.g., availability target for hosted vs private.
[04:52] Jamie Liu: hosted has a 99.9% SLA for paid tiers; dedicated/private SLA is contract-defined — we can put a generic note and link to dedicated contract.

[05:03] Ari Patel: process question: what's the validation flow? aurora validation team runs smoke tests in our sandbox and expects an infra playbook.
[05:11] Carlos Mendes: recommended flow: (1) Redwood shares ref-arch + terraform + quickstart; (2) Aurora deploys to sandbox and runs test plan (we'll provide test harness); (3) Redwood runs a connectivity and security checklist; (4) sign-off and move to production listing. we aim for 5-7 business days if both teams are blocked-free.

[05:32] Priya Rao: on SSO we need SAML metadata and whether you support provisioning via SCIM.
[05:38] Jamie Liu: we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning as an enterprise feature. we'll include sample SAML metadata and endpoint URLs in the security doc share.

[05:50] Leah Kim: about the reference arch diagram — can you show data flow for both hosted and private with where KMS lives and where logs flow?
[05:58] Carlos Mendes: yes i'll include both flows. hosted: customer traffic -> aurora marketplace -> redwood public api (with optional private connector) -> redwood runtime -> model; logs flow into redwood-managed log store and can be exported to aurora s3. private: customer traffic -> aurora infra -> peered redwood endpoint in customer VPC -> redwood runtime running in customer-controlled infra (or in aurora-managed cluster) with KMS keys controlled by aurora.

[06:28] Jamie Liu: quick note about model variants in marketplace listing — we can list recommended default models and note compatibility/quantization; customers can switch to a higher-latency lower-cost variant. we should document recommended profile for common use-cases.

[06:45] Tom O'Neill: can we call out a default "developer" SKU and an "enterprise" SKU in listing? dev for hosted, enterprise for private/dedicated?
[06:54] Jamie Liu: yep that's how others do it. we'll propose SKU names and pricing tiers in the PRD.

[07:05] Ari Patel: co-marketing — aurora wants a joint press and blog around the listing. what's realistic for PR timing?
[07:12] Jamie Liu: if we hit sandbox validation by 2026-08-31 we can prepare assets and tentatively aim for a joint blog + press the second week of September. can't promise exact window until validation completes.

[07:23] Priya Rao: any third-party dependencies or vendors we should call out (e.g., for KMS/HSM or metric exports)?

[07:31] Carlos Mendes: we typically rely on cloud-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK) or HSM integration for on-prem. metric export uses s3 or push via webhook into aurora's billing system. we'll document supported endpoints and auth methods.

[07:49] Jamie Liu: Tom, can you describe marketplace listing meta constraints — image sizes, description limits, contact person?
[07:56] Tom O'Neill: sure — 3 images max, 1200x600 px recommended, 500 char short description, up to 2000 char long description, contact email + 1 tech contact. also needs a security questionnaire filled out.

[08:13] Ari Patel: ok we'll gather the marketing assets. Priya will handle the security questionnaire with redwood's docs.

[08:21] Carlos Mendes: two technical questions from our side: 1) do you require marketplace to host a one-click deploy as part of listing or is a manual quickstart acceptable? 2) for private deployments do you require full support handoff from aurora operations?
[08:33] Tom O'Neill: marketplace strongly prefers a one-click if it's a deployable template, but for reference integrations a quickstart is acceptable. for private, ops handoff is negotiated per listing, we typically require an on-call contact during validation.

[08:48] Priya Rao: security Q: does redwood support customer-managed KMS for model weights and also TLS termination in-customer?
[08:56] Carlos Mendes: yes we support BYOK for disk & model encryption, and TLS termination can be in-customer with our private endpoint pattern. details in the runbook.

[09:05] Jamie Liu: circling back to timeline and owners — i'll send the security artifacts and SOC2 slides by tomorrow EOD; carlos will push the initial ref-arch repo and terraform snippets by 2026-08-26; ari will provide listing metadata by 2026-08-21.

[09:23] Ari Patel: sounds good. one more scheduling ask — can we do infra runbook deep-dive with priya next week?

[09:29] Carlos Mendes: yes i'll block 60 minutes — propose 2026-08-25 14:00 UTC, will send calendar invite.

[09:36] Tom O'Neill: for validations we'll need a test harness — simple smoke tests for API auth, key rotation, and throughput check, can you provide that?
[09:44] Carlos Mendes: yes we'll include a test harness (postman + python pytest) in the repo and a sample results sheet.

[09:53] Priya Rao: on data residency — some customers will require EU-only data processing; does redwood support regional hosting?
[09:59] Jamie Liu: yes we have regional endpoints and can route EU traffic to EU-hosted clusters; we'll add a regional hosting section to the ref-arch.

[10:10] Ari Patel: okay let's recap next steps and owners.

[10:14] Jamie Liu: recap: 1) Jamie to send security docs and SOC2/ISO slides (due 2026-08-20), 2) Carlos to push ref-arch + terraform + benchmark sheet (due 2026-08-26), 3) Ari to send marketplace metadata and logos (due 2026-08-21), 4) Priya to share SAML metadata & security questionnaire answers (due 2026-08-24), 5) schedule infra runbook deep-dive 2026-08-25 14:00 UTC.

[10:41] Tom O'Neill: ok thanks all, we'll aim to submit sandbox listing asap once we have the artifacts.

[10:46] Jamie Liu: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with PRD and repo links, talk soon.

End of transcript.
